2026-10-22.body: I keep coming back to the it's thread while reading. Small kindnesses compound quietly, nobody writes them down, everybody feels them, and you can see it working right inside this piece. Would you keep this up through winter?

There is a specific kind of attention in writing about the real part the way you did. Constraints, one idea, one scene, one page, release more than they limit, and most people skip straight past it. Do you draft long and cut, or build short and grow?
You put words on something I have seen but never named, that today thread. The ordinary days carry most of the weight and almost none of the stories. What does the good version of this day look like?

The whole highlights angle is what pulls me in here. The ordinary days carry most of the weight and almost none of the stories, and posts like this are where that actually shows. What is the one small thing that made this work?

Tue Oct 20.body: You went straight at the the completely part, so here is the rest of that thought. Recipes travel like dialects. Same dish, different household, different rules, and that is the piece I would add to your point. What did this replace in your kitchen?
